iOS 27 has arrived, with the biggest highlights being Siri AI and several new Apple Intelligence features. However, one of my favourite new features lets you quickly paste content from your iPhone clipboard, which is incredibly handy. Here's how it works.

iOS 27 adds a paste shortcut above the keyboard, giving you one-tap access to the clipboard

Apple adds a huge number of new features to iOS every year, and this year's upgrades include Apple Wallet, Messages, CarPlay, and more.

Plenty of new features that the average iPhone user might easily overlook.

But there's one new feature in iOS 27 that I expect readers will use all the time.

When you copy text to your iPhone clipboard—whether it's a link or a photo—as soon as you open a new text input field, iOS 27 will display a paste shortcut above the keyboard.

The concept is simple: if you've copied something and immediately switch to another app, or open another text field, Apple knows there's a good chance you want to paste it there.

The system no longer requires you to open the copy/paste menu and then tap paste—instead, it automatically shows a paste suggestion above the keyboard, done with one tap.

You can also preview your clipboard content in real time in the top row of the keyboard. If it's text, you'll see the content; if it's an image, you'll see a small thumbnail preview.

This is the kind of feature I wouldn't have asked for myself, but during my time testing the iOS 27 beta over the summer, I found it genuinely very convenient in everyday life.

Have you used the new paste shortcut in iOS 27? Feel free to share in the comments.
